current_leader.name: Processor native-currency settlement optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: foreign-currency processor balance appears -> matching settlement account availability and PSP fee schedule are known -> compare native payout cost against conversion and expected same-currency obligations -> recommend keep-native or convert -> measure avoided FX/payout fees
current_leader.why_survived: Stripe still exposes a deterministic no-conversion state when a payout currency has an eligible matching bank account, while unsupported currencies are converted to the account default. Multi-currency settlement itself can carry roughly 1% payout fees and instant currency conversion starts around 0.5%, so the decision has a measurable dollar consequence. No exact lightweight read-only product was found that combines PSP balances, PSP fee schedules and external same-currency obligations to continuously recommend native settlement versus conversion. However, recurrence after competent static setup is not yet proven strongly enough to keep leakage as PASS.
strongest_evidence: Stripe documentation: payout in a currency with available bank account/debit card causes no conversion; without one Stripe converts the balance to the default currency.
Stripe current pricing: multi-currency settlement is generally around 1% in supported markets; instant currency conversion starts around 0.5%.
Stripe NetSuite connector explicitly describes using multiple settlement accounts to avoid currency conversion fees.
current_leader.closest_threat: Broad multi-currency treasury/payment systems increasingly hold, convert and route balances natively; Pockyt explicitly markets holding 27 currencies and paying suppliers in native currency, while Stripe itself supplies the settlement primitives. The wedge survives only as a read-only optimization layer if external obligations cause the optimal keep-native/convert decision to change often enough.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read-only: ingest authorized PSP balances by currency, configured settlement accounts, processor conversion/native-payout fees, and upcoming AP/card obligations by currency; output KEEP NATIVE or CONVERT with expected deterministic fee difference. Do not execute FX, payouts or hold funds.
current_leader.monetization: Small fee per economically valuable currency decision, per-currency-month pricing, or capped percentage of verified PSP FX/payout fees avoided, benchmarked against a competent static multi-currency setup.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: A one-time setup of matching USD/EUR/GBP settlement accounts may capture most savings. If dynamic optimization adds little after that baseline, the recurring tollbooth disappears.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify the incremental savings of dynamic obligation-aware decisions after best-practice static multi-currency setup. Search merchant case data where currency mix and foreign-currency obligations vary enough to change the optimal settlement choice month to month. If dynamic delta is small, reject and promote merchant settlement acceleration or a new event-level candidate.

runner_ups.note: Clean fee delta and recurring processor event, but unnecessary paid acceleration volume remains unquantified.
Programmable and measurable, but dynamic savings beyond best static tuning remain unproven.
Strong general mechanism, still lacks one defensible high-value non-AI vertical.

rejections.fatal_flaw: Exact incumbents already detect undercharged/uncharged/expiring OTA virtual cards and recover them on performance pricing; current products report roughly $9k-$13k annual recovery per property and dedicated automated VCC recovery.
Multiple exact products now parse carrier statements, compare expected vs actual commissions, flag missing/underpaid amounts and support recovery workflows.
Exact incumbents and first-party travel products already monitor refundable reservations and auto-rebook when prices fall.
Current contingency-fee and continuous-audit products already compare contracts to SaaS/vendor invoices and recover pricing drift, missed discounts and duplicate charges.

new_search_rules: For configuration optimizers, score only incremental recurring savings after competent static setup; do not count one-time cleanup value as recurring leakage.
High leakage plus perfect triggers are insufficient when performance-fee incumbents already own the exact recovery workflow.
Prefer event-level state transitions whose optimal action can genuinely change from one event to the next rather than stable account configuration.
